proposals.note: Ring of RZZ gates (alternating a1/a2) ensures Z-basis correlations flow along all 6 edges of the cycle, directly feeding the Z_iZ_j readout. Three CRZ chord gates (0,3),(1,4),(2,5) with tied param d1 add long-range entanglement across the graph diameter. Alternating single-qubit RY (b1/b2) and RZ (c1/c2) rotations provide local expressivity while preserving Z3 cyclic symmetry (shift-by-2). The Z3 invariance matches the bipartite structure of K6 and regularizes the 7-parameter block. RZZ is chosen over CNOT/CZ for the ring because it commutes with the diagonal readout basis, giving cleaner gradient signal for connectivity detection.

proposals.note: Block is exactly equivariant under the involution sigma=(0,3)(1,4)(2,5) (order-2 group). Structure: RY layer, then five RZZ layers each forming a sigma-invariant perfect matching of the 6-qubit ring (11 of 15 pairs covered), then a partial RZ layer. Each matching consists of disjoint pairs so intra-layer gates commute; each matching is setwise-fixed by sigma, guaranteeing sigma*U*sigma_dag=U. The 4 uncovered pairs (1,2),(1,5),(2,4),(4,5) receive indirect entanglement via the 4x block repetitions and feature-map re-encoding. 6 trainable RZZ angles give rich phase structure for detecting global connectivity.

proposals.note: Six-cycle equivariant block: RY(a) on all 6 qubits, RZZ(p) on the 6-cycle edges (0-1-2-3-4-5-0), RZ(b) on all 6 qubits, RZZ(d) on the 3 diametrically-opposite pairs (0-3,1-4,2-5). The 6-cycle permutation maps each gate orbit to itself with identical parameters, guaranteeing exact equivariance. RZZ on cycle edges builds nearest-neighbour ZZ correlations that feed directly into the Z_iZ_j readout observables; the 3 diagonal RZZ gates capture long-range (distance-3) correlations needed to detect connectivity across the full graph. Four tied parameters keep the hypothesis space small and regularised, while the two-layer, two-repeat structure (4 block applications total) provides sufficient depth to propagate connectivity information across all six nodes. Compared to c0005 (7 params, CRZ-based), this trades a few parameters for a provably valid 6-cycle symmetry that should reduce overfitting on the connectivity task, whose labels are invariant under any node relabeling.

proposals.note: Cyclic-shift (Z6) equivariant block: RY(t1) on all 6 qubits, RZZ(t2) on 6 adjacent cycle edges, RZ(t3) on all 6, CRZ(t4) on 6 directed cycle edges. Every gate orbit is closed under the shift 0->1->2->3->4->5->0, so P^dag U P = U exactly. Previous verifier failure (residual 0.81) came from a gate list whose orbits were not closed; here each gate type appears on a full orbit with a single tied parameter, guaranteeing equivariance. The task (graph connectivity) is S6-symmetric, so the Z6 subgroup is a safe, verifiable subset. 24 gates, 4 params, 4 entangling layers per block application; with 2 layers x 2 repeats the block is applied 4 times, giving enough depth for information to propagate around the cycle and detect disconnections.

proposals.note: Replaced CRZ entangling with RZZ on both cycle edges (dist-1) and skip-one edges (dist-2), covering 12/15 graph edges per block application. This gives the block more direct access to longer-range connectivity information without needing as many sequential layers to propagate. Tied 4 parameters (one per gate class) to limit overfitting. Kept cyclic symmetry hypothesis since label-preservation is exact; equivariance residual is expected due to fixed feature-map breaking the symmetry, but the structural bias toward cyclic invariance still regularizes training. Compared to c0008 (CRZ+RZZ on cycle only), the distance-2 RZZ adds a second entangling range that lets the block detect paths of length 2 in a single application, reducing the effective depth needed for connectivity detection.

proposals.note: Cyclic C6-invariant block. All same-type gates are grouped so that the cyclic shift permutes each group onto itself; since RY gates commute with each other, RZ gates commute with each other, and all RZZ gates are diagonal (mutually commuting), the block is exactly invariant under the 6-cycle. Two RZZ orbits (nearest-neighbor and distance-2 pairs) give 12 entangling gates capturing local and mid-range graph structure; the single-qubit RY/RZ layers provide rotation freedom. Four tied parameters keep the model compact while the feature-map re-uploading (2 layers x 2 repeats) supplies depth. This replaces the prior CRZ+RZZ mix with pure RZZ to guarantee commutativity within each group and eliminate the large channel residual seen before.

proposals.note: Designed around a provably-equivariant Z2xZ2xZ2 structure under (01)(23)(45). Gates are grouped into four blocks (RY, RZ, RZZ, CZ) whose products are each individually invariant under the permutation: single-qubit gates share params and commute within block; RZZ self-invariant pairs (0,1),(2,3),(4,5) are symmetric; paired RZZ gates (0,2)<->(1,3), (0,4)<->(1,5), (2,4)<->(3,5) are disjoint and commute so the permuted product equals the original; CZ is symmetric. Entangling graph covers 12 of 15 node-pairs (all except (0,3),(1,2),(2,5)), giving dense connectivity detection across 2 layers x 2 repeats. 6 trainable params balance expressivity with regularization. Prior c0008 (risk 0.37) used a similar cycle+CRZ structure but its 6-cycle hypothesis failed equivariance (residual ~0.81); this design uses a smaller group that is exactly realized at the gate-product level.

proposals.note: Builds on c0008 (best dev risk 0.3697) with same 4-param/24-gate RY+RZ+RZZ+CRZ skeleton but swaps the entangling topology and the claimed symmetry generator. RZZ pairs form a connected subgraph (triangle 0-1-2 plus edges 0-3,2-3,1-4) while CRZ pairs add directed control flow (0→1,2→1,0→3,2→3,1→4,3→5). Hypothesis is transposition swap(0,2) (order-2 group); all gate sets are closed under this swap and parameters are fully tied within each gate type, so the block is equivariant. The connected RZZ+CRZ topology mirrors the connectivity question: information propagates along edges to detect whether all six nodes belong to one component. Four tied parameters keep the block compact and regularized, matching the best-performing prior structure.
